cards.title: Hour 14 has a concentrated error spike
cards.detail: Hour 14 recorded 1,460 errors in 9,225 requests, an error rate of 15.83%, versus 709 errors in 195,768 requests across the other hours, or 0.36%. Investigate the hour-14 deployment, dependency, or traffic segment.

cards.title: Caller-07 has an unusually high unit cost
cards.detail: Caller-07 spent $174.12 on 1,180 requests, or $0.1476 per request, compared with $0.0164 overall, about 9.0 times higher. Check its model selection, token volume, or request configuration.

cards.title: Caller-01 dominates traffic and spend
cards.detail: Caller-01 generated 105,832 requests, 51.6% of total traffic, and $1,643.86 of spend, 49.0% of the total. It also produced 952 errors, 43.9% of all errors, so it is the highest-leverage caller for cost and reliability controls.

cards.title: Ten callers show systematically weak cache performance
cards.detail: Callers 03, 05, 07, 09, 11, 13, 15, 17, 21, and 23 handled 44,951 requests and $849.66 of spend while reporting cache-hit rates from 3.7% to 8.9%; the other regular callers range from 82.3% to 88.8%. Inspect cache keys, eligibility, and configuration for this cohort.

cards.title: Model-alpha is the main latency bottleneck
cards.detail: Model-alpha handled 86,080 requests and $1,409.02, about 42.0% of both total requests and spend, while having the highest meaningful-model p95 latency at 2,454 ms. Review routing and prompt or payload characteristics before directing additional traffic to it.
